title: Inductance, LR and LC circuits
qualification: AP Physics C: Electricity and Magnetism
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics C: Electricity and Magnetism (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: MG09-calc-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; MG09-calc-2#t2 term and clue written for the game; MG09-calc-2#t1 term and clue written for the game; MG09-calc-1#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: MG09-calc-1#N.7, MG09-calc-2#N.2, MG09-calc-1#N.9, MG09-calc-2#N.6, MG09-calc-2#N.9.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Henry
items.clue: Unit equal to 1 V s/A or 1 Wb/A.

items.label: Loop rule
items.clue: Gives ε = IR + L dI/dt for a battery, resistor and coil in series.

items.label: Time constant
items.clue: The ratio L/R: after it, the current reaches about 63% of its final value.

items.label: Inductor
items.clue: A coil with significant L; an ideal one has no emf across it at steady current.

questions.stem: Three long air-core solenoids have these properties. Solenoid 1: N turns, length ℓ, cross-sectional area A. Solenoid 2: 2N turns, length 2ℓ, area A. Solenoid 3: N turns, length ℓ/2, area A/2. Which ranks their inductances L₁, L₂ and L₃?

A series circuit contains an ideal 9.0 V battery, a 25 Ω resistor, an ideal inductor and a switch. The switch is closed at t = 0. At a later instant, the current in the circuit is 0.24 A. What is the magnitude of the potential difference across the inductor at that instant?

An ideal inductor of inductance 0.50 H, connected only to a resistor, carries a current of 4.0 A. The current then decreases to 2.0 A. How much energy does the resistor dissipate while the current decreases?

A series circuit contains an ideal battery of emf ε, a resistor of resistance R, an ideal inductor of inductance L and a switch. The switch is closed at t = 0. At what time t is the energy stored in the inductor one-quarter of its final value?

An ideal inductor of inductance 0.40 H carries a steady current of 4.0 A. At t = 0 a switch disconnects the battery and, at the same instant, connects the inductor across a 12 Ω resistor, so the current decays in the loop formed by the inductor and the resistor. How much energy is dissipated in the resistor between t = 0 and t = τ, where τ is the time constant of that loop?
